title: Scenario Reduction for Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
summary: Two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs are important tools for decision-making under uncertainty. Representing the uncertainty with many scenarios, however, can make them challenging to solve. Scenario reduction addresses this by finding a distribution supported on fewer scenarios that still yields similar optimal first-stage decisions. In this paper, we revisit the classical scenario reduction theory based on distances between probability distributions and the optimal mass transportation problem.
